rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a person shares another’s welfare and harm as their own, social feeling and brotherhood begin; practiced empathy strengthens community and reduces pride.
rows.anchor: Bir vicdanda bu mahabbet u mehâfet yükselip de bir diğerini dahi kendisi gibi, lâekal kendisine müsâvî bir kıymetle görmeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The breadth and strength of shared feeling set the scale of brotherhood, society, and civilization; narrow particular affiliations fragment wider bonds.
rows.anchor: Bu his, bu câmi‘a ne kadar vüs‘at peydâ eder ve ne kadar kuvve bulursa kibir o nisbette tenâkus eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A community needs both breadth in its common bond and strength in conscience: breadth without strength dissolves it, while strength without breadth prevents its growth.
rows.anchor: Câmi‘ada vüs‘at var da vicdanda kuvvet yoksa o cem‘iyyet idare edilemez, dağılmaya, küçülmeye mahkum olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Social feeling is first a divine innate gift and second a reflection of one's surroundings, and it is shaped by both innate and acquired upbringing.
rows.anchor: Bu rûh-i ictimâ‘înin teessüsü evvelemirde fıtratta bir mevhibe-i rabbâniye ve derece-i sâniyede muhîtin bir in‘ikâsıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God, without counterpart, equal, or partner, can encompass all human love and fear; devotion to Him grounds universal brotherhood and a worldwide community.
rows.anchor: Şerîki, nazîri mevcud olmayan da ancak Hak teâlâ’dır. Çünkü mukabili li-zâtihi bâtıl ve li-zâtihi mümteni‘olan ancak O’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God trains and strengthens social feeling by taking a covenant from each rational individual in the plural, so each represents all humanity and the worlds.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da Hak teâlâ kendisini evvelâ zevi’l-‘ukūl ferdlere duyurarak vicdanlarında bu rûh-i ictimâ‘îyi terbiye ve takviye etmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person plural is grammatically spoken by one individual who represents fellow believers; a congregation speaks through a representative rather than each member saying “I.”
rows.anchor: çünkü cemi‘mütekellim, muhatab ve gāib cemi‘lere benzemez, bunda hakikaten söyleyen yine bir müfreddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “we worship” makes the individual represent those he feels as brothers, beginning with guardian angels and extending to present or envisaged congregations.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh cemi‘mütekellim hakikatte nefs-i mütekellim me‘a’l-gayr demektir. Ve bu suretle إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ diyen bir ferd olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the author's school, followers behind the prayer leader recite neither Fatiha nor anything else because the imam recites for them; a person praying alone recites as imam of a potential congregation.
rows.anchor: mezhebimizde imamın arkasında namaz kılan cemaat ne Fâtiha ne sâire hiçbir şey kıraat etmez de hepsinin hesabına imam okur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As like-minded individuals meet, an actual congregation forms readily and follows an imam; its collective power corresponds to that imam.
rows.anchor: bu gibi ferdler tekessür edip tanıştıkça bilfiil cemaat de kendiliğinden ve kolayca teşekkül ediverir de derhâl içlerinden birini imam tanıyarak ona iktidâ ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Social spirit precedes the social body, so an individual can carry and represent the conscience of a community before it exists without circularity.
rows.anchor: rûh-i ictimâ‘î, cism-i ictimâ‘îye mütekaddim olduğundan bir ferd, bir cemaatin bütün vicdânını onun teşekkülünden evvel dahi taşıyarak onu temsil eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is an unsurpassed social and civil bond; narrow-minded people seek small gods and think restricted brotherhood easier, yet cannot attain a Muslim's firmness and serenity.
rows.anchor: İşte İslâm bu büyük ve lâ-nazîr rûh-i ictimâ‘îdir ve onun muhtevî olduğu ma‘nâ-yı ictimâ‘î ve medenî fevkinde hiçbir câmi‘a tasavvuruna imkân bulunamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslim community's strength depends on the number of its members and the strength of their Islamic conscience; sustaining this universal spirit without an existing community is a prophetic station, especially that of the final Prophet, by divine support.
rows.anchor: bu makam makām-ı enbiyâ ve bilhassa makām-ı Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first established this covenant in Muhammad's prophetic heart through revelation; he is the complete, truthful servant and representative individual able fully to say the verse, and the model of servanthood.
rows.anchor: tam mânasıyla إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diyebilen sâdık ve masdûk ‘abd-i ekmel, ferd-i câmi‘, Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Efendimiz’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faith declaration pairs God's oneness with Muhammad's being His servant and messenger; at Hira the Prophet's worship represented the universal spirit and his communal conscience became imam to all worlds.
rows.anchor: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلٰهَ إِلاَّ اللّٰهّٰ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ düstûr-ı îmânı teşkil eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities sincerely following the Prophet's Sunna can collectively uphold the covenant, submit to no one besides God, and seek aid from no one else; this spirit drove early Islamic conquests and expansion.
rows.anchor: bu ‘akd-i ‘ubûdiyeti bihakkın söyleyebilmişler, ne Allah’tan başkasına boyun eğmişler ne de ‘arz-ı isti‘âne eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing the plural with singular wording in prayer invalidates it because God requires a communal conscience covenant, not an individual-only promise; worshippers should consider whom they represent and on whose behalf they seek aid.
rows.anchor: Çünkü Cenâb-ı Allah ferdden sade vicdân-ı ferdîsiyle bir mîsâk istemiyor da vicdân-ı ictimâ‘î ile bir mîsâk istiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no actual worshipping congregation suffices, a Muslim should mentally join the existing congregation to the potential one, including God's angels.
rows.anchor: mevcud olan cemaate kuvvedeki cemaati, Allah’ın melâikesini dahi zammetmeyi her hâlde unutmamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes say the plural pronouns refer to the reciter together with guardian angels, the present congregation, or all monotheists.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn buradaki “biz” zamirlerini okuyan kimse ile beraberindeki hafaza melâikesine veyahut cemâ‘at-i hâzıraya veyahut bütün muvahhidîne râci‘dir derler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse entails both unity of Lordship, accepting God's unique real essence, and unity of worship, a pledge to form a unified community; the latter builds a relational unity on the former.
rows.anchor: hem tevhîd-i rubûbiyete ve hem tevhîd-i ‘ubûdiyete delâlet etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse renews a witnessed testimony that there is no deity besides God and a commitment to act on it; collective Qur'anic pledges can distribute rights and duties to every individual (an individual obligation) or assign them to the collective body (a communal obligation).
rows.anchor: cemiyeti ferdde, ferdi cemiyette indirâc ettirerek her ferde ‘ale’s-seviyye hak ve vazife tevzî‘etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the individual sense is retained: each believer bears the individual obligation, while collective testimony is the aggregate of individual testimony; the two consciences mutually guarantee one another.
rows.anchor: İslâm’da hem ferdin ve hem cemaatin vicdânî tevhîdi vardır. Ve bunlar mütekābilen yekdiğerinin kefîlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is pure monotheism and rejects every form of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: bunda envâ‘-i şirkin hepsini nefyeden bir cevâb-ı red vardır

rows.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
rows.claim: Razi classifies shirk by corporeal versus incorporeal partners: lower or celestial bodies, simple or composite bodies, and material idols, plants, animals, humans, heavenly bodies, or spirits.
rows.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî burada şu telhîsi yapmıştır: “Müşrikler bölük bölüktürler. Çünkü Allah teâlâ’ya karşı iddia edip taptıkları

rows.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
rows.claim: Razi includes worshippers of fire, the sun, moon, stars, and astrologers who attribute fortune and misfortune to the stars, as well as Manichaean light-and-dark dualists.
rows.anchor: Ecsâm-ı ‘ulviyeden şerîk ittihaz edenler de Güneş, Ay ve sâir yıldızlar gibi kevâkibe tapan ve saâdet u nuhûseti onlara atfeden Sâbi’e ve ekser-i müneccimîndir

rows.speaker: امام فخرالدین رازی
rows.claim: Razi describes angel worshippers who assign cosmic and climatic governance to spirits and worship their images, and dualists who posit good and evil first principles such as Yazdan and Ahriman.
rows.anchor: bunlara “‘abede-i melâike” denir. Bunlar mâneviyâtı sezmiş ve fakat ecsâm-perest, ‘abede-i esnâm menzilesinde kalmışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two wholly disconnected first principles could not organize one world; if they share kinship or a higher principle, they cease to be first principles, which leads toward the Trinity and Christianity's developed form.
rows.anchor: aralarında asla bir nokta-i ittisal ve iştirak bulunmayacak olan iki mebde’-i evvelin bir nizam tesis edemeyecekleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity wandered from awareness of one God into multiplicity, reduced it to two and then Trinity; Islam restores true oneness, and the verse refutes shirk, uniting people who enter Islam while departure fragments and humiliates them.
rows.anchor: nihâyet dîn-i İslâm ile tevhîd-i hakīkīyi kemâliyle bulmuş ve toplanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the covenant, the prayer for guidance begins as the most comprehensive practical application of seeking divine aid; it answers the worshipper's need, after pausing at “we seek aid,” to know where and how to begin.
rows.anchor: Bu talep ve dua isti‘ânenin ehem ve eşmel bir sûret-i tatbîkiyesiyle beyânıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is contained in seeking aid, which is contained in worship and praise; thus all of Fatiha unfolds as one complete الحمد لله sentence and unified discourse, so its first two pauses are complete but not obligatory.
rows.anchor: bütün Fâtiha’nın bir اَلْحَمْدُ للّٰهِِّٰ cümle-i tâmmesinin inkişâfı olup sade başıyla değil hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla kelâm-ı vâhid hâlinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command form becomes an imperative from higher to lower, a supplication from lower to higher, and a request between equals.
rows.anchor: Bu sîga ile yukarıdan aşağıya büyükten küçüğe cezmen vukū‘bulan taleb-i fiile “emir”, aşağıdan yukarıya yapılan talebe “dua”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance gently and delicately indicates how to reach a desired destination: it may show the way, take someone along it, or lead them all the way; showing is non-arriving direction (irshad), while taking there is tawfiq.
rows.anchor: “Hidâyet” matlûba îsâl edecek şeye lutf u letâfetle delâlet etmektir ki yolu sadece gösterivermek veya yola götürüvermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance concerns a good goal and gentle method; applying it to an evil destination, as in the direction to Hell, is figurative sarcasm or insinuation.
rows.anchor: Hidâyet matlûb-i hayra mahsustur. Meselâ hırsıza yol göstermeye, rehberlik etmeye “hidâyet” denilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best Turkish rendering is the familiar “bize hidâyet et”: “show” omits leading, “take” omits gentleness, and replacing an established word with a strained alternative distorts the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh ٱهْدِنَا’nın meâlinde en muvâfık tâbir lisânımızda mâruf olduğu gibi “bize hidâyet et” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine guidance is innumerable in both its particular forms and its kinds, but can be considered under four ordered general categories.
rows.anchor: ‘add u ihsâ olmadığı gibi envâ‘ı itibariyle de öyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind is bestowing and sustaining spiritual or bodily powers, senses, reason, will, and the natural or animal faculties that serve human needs, and aligning intentions with desires.
rows.anchor: havâss-ı zâhire ve bâtınesini, kuvve-i akliye ve irâdiyesini ve hatta ef‘âl-i tabî‘iye ve hayvâniyesinin sudûruna sebep olan kuvâ-yı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind establishes proofs that distinguish truth from falsehood and right conduct from corruption; the Thamud were shown guidance but preferred blindness.
rows.anchor: Hak ile bâtılı, salâh ile fesâdı fark ettiren delâil nasb u ikāme etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third kind guides through sending messengers and revealing scriptures, as with divinely guided leaders and the Qur'an's guidance to the soundest way.
rows.anchor: İrsâl-i rusül ve inzâl-i kütüb ile hidâyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth, special guidance unveils hidden realities to hearts through revelation, inspiration, or true dreams, especially for prophets and saints; others have a limited share below certainty, and guidance can also be summarized as inner or outer, creational or revealed.
rows.anchor: Vahiy veya ilham veya rü’yâ-yı sâdıka gibi fevkalâde tarîklerle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contextual setting determines which sense of guidance a Qur'anic occurrence carries.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da “hidâyet” kelimesi kullanıldığı zaman, bunlardan hangisi murad olunabileceğini makamına göre anlamak iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may take its second object directly, as here, or with ilā; some grammarians explain the direct form as eliding the preposition for arrival, from an underlying “guide us to the path.”
rows.anchor: Hidâyet mef‘ûl-i sânîsine kâh إل� ile, bazen de burada olduğu gibi bizzat ta‘diye eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance and being guided are related; those already guided ask for steadfastness or a higher degree, while the previously unled ask to attain the basic guidance.
rows.anchor: hidâyette bulunanların hidâyet istemesi de sebat veya ziyâde-i mertebe istemek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article on “the path” may mark a known covenant path belonging to God, or the generic class of road that metaphorically applies to God's path.
rows.anchor: Hidâyetin ikinci mef‘ûlü, yani mef‘ûlün ileyhi olan ٱلصِّرَٰطَ lâm-ı ‘ahd ile صراطك “senin sırâtın” terkîb-i izâfîsinin mânasını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readings use ṣād as the Quraysh form, smoother and more eloquent due to emphatic sounds; Qunbul from Ibn Kathir and Ruways from Yaqub transmit sīn, while Hamza's ishmām hints at zāy in the Qays dialect (as Abu Hayyan reports).
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr’den Kunbul ve Ya‘kūb’dan Rüveys rivayetlerinde de böyle sin ile es-sirât (السراط), sirât okunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Arabic “sirat” means a great, busy highway, Turkish speakers know it as the required afterlife bridge over Hell; the text hints at that image and Amr ibn Ubayd transmitted that interpretation, but exegetes take its primary intent as a representative metaphor for truth and Islam.
rows.anchor: Lâkin burada asıl murad bir isti‘âre-i temsîliye ile tarîk-i hak ve millet-i İslâm olduğunu müfessirîn-i kirâm beyan edegelmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic terms distinguish general road (tarīq), traveled road (sabīl), and busy, straight, great, or clear ways (including sirat and sharia); “sirat” therefore evokes sharia.
rows.anchor: Lügat-ı Arab’da ‘ale’l-ıtlâk yola “tarîk”, işlek yola “sebîl”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqim means completely straight with no bend; because a road may still slope, the adjective adds flatness, so “straight” alone does not fully convey it, though Turkish also uses it for true or truthful.
rows.anchor: “Müstakīm”, hiçbir yerinde meyil ve eğrilik bulunmayan dümdüz ve dosdoğru demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic rhetoric includes at least sixteen theoretically established categorical modes; suggestive, non-categorical rhetorical nuances are grasped through rhetoric's innumerable aesthetic judgments.
rows.anchor: Vücûh-i beyan kat‘iyyet nokta-i nazarıyla lâekal on altı vechi ihtivâ ettiği usûlen mâlumdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chance is only an appearance to the ignorant; divine wisdom has no chance, and every choice by the all-wise has a weighting wisdom even though God's will is not externally compelled.
rows.anchor: Tesadüf müşâhede-i esrardan gāfil olan câhilin nazarındadır. Hikmette tesadüf yoktur ve Hakîm-i mutlakın her ihtiyârında bir hikmet-i mürecciha vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To interpret Qur'anic wording, establish each word's sense, compare related alternatives, consider syntax and context, then distinguish intended meaning from rhetorical embellishment; separate a term's mental sense from its real referents, since this affects legal inference.
rows.anchor: evvelâ kelimelerin mefhumlarını iyice tesbit etmek, sâniyen mevki‘lerinde lafzen ve mânen alâkadar olabileceği kelimât ve me‘ânîsi ile mukayese eylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators transmit definitions including God's path, truth, a balanced way, God's Book, faith and its entailments, Islam and its law, the Prophet's and leading Companions' path, Sunna and the community, Paradise's road, and the bridge over Hell; investigators synthesize truth's path and Islam.
rows.anchor: Tefsirlere baktığımız zaman ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ’den murad ne olduğu hakkında şu rivayetleri görürüz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the definite article's covenant or generic force, most transmitted explanations concern referents and some concern the concept; aside from Hell's bridge, they describe the same referent by attributes, so confusing sense with referent creates false disagreements.
rows.anchor: Cisr-i cehennem istisna edilirse öbürleri vâki‘de aynı medlûlün evsâfından biriyle ifadesinden başka bir şey olmadıkları hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The investigators' synthesis distinguishes concept from referent: “path of truth” gives the concept and Islam gives its real-world instance.
rows.anchor: Tarîk-i hak mefhum, millet-i İslâm mâsadaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second mention of “path” explains the first by apposition, which can be whole or partial; the intended focus remains the apposition, while the first phrase prepares and reinforces the meaning rather than being discarded.
rows.anchor: “صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ”, ٱلصِّرَٰطَ’tan bedeldir. Bedel-i kül veya ba‘z olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following appositional clauses clarify the path's essence and attributes: those whom God favored, those not under anger, and those not astray.
rows.anchor: sırât-ı müstakīmin hem zâtını ve hem vasfını şerh u tavzih eden kayıtlar vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full appositional construction must be considered before the intended meaning and referent of the straight path can be determined.
rows.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ’den murad olan mâna ve mâsadak bunların hey’et-i mecmû‘ası mülâhaza edildikten sonra ta‘ayyün edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically the term means a straight, level highway, but the discourse concerns seeking aid, an immaterial matter, so it must mean a spiritual road or explicitly include one figuratively.
rows.anchor: Bu ise gayr-i mahsüs bir mânadır. Binâen‘aleyh bu karîne-i kat‘iyye ile biz anlarız ki bu yol manevî yoldur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor first imagines a clear, broad, busy, straight physical road, then a clear and comprehensive God-appointed intellectual and practical law safely directing human thought and action toward good goals, and finally uses “straight path” for that spiritual reality, clarified by “guide us.”
rows.anchor: bizi doğruca ve selâmetle hayırlı muradlarımıza götürecek ilmî, amelî, vâzıh ve şümullü ve Hak teâlâ’nın vaz‘ı olan bir kānûn-ı hak tasavvur ediyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether every path that qualifies generally as a path of truth belongs to the requested straight path remains a question requiring consideration.
rows.anchor: tarîk-i hak ıtlâkına sezâ olan her tarîk, matlub olan tarîk-i müstakīme dâhil midir, değil midir?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the preceding plea seeks aid, the first and most important request is guidance to a clear path that elicits divine aid; the passage therefore asks for God's most important assistance first.
rows.anchor: ibtidâ me‘ûnet-i ilâhiyenin ehemm u akdemini taleb etmemizi telkin ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth's broad meaning can encompass paths that lead to evil relative to created aims: each divine law leads to an objective, and some paths lead to God's pleasure while others lead to His wrath.
rows.anchor: lâkin birisi rızâsına götürür, biri de gazabına götürür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested path must therefore be defined as the path leading to God's pleasure; “the straight path” conveys a more specific and clearer meaning than the broad notion of a path of truth, and its appositional expansion identifies it fully with Islam.
rows.anchor: İşte bütün bu ibhamları izâle için bedelin tezyîliyle mefhûmun mütenâveli tefsir veya tahsis olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is Lord of all worlds, His laws operate in every realm; laws may be named for their maker or their subject, but “divine laws” and “God's way” are more accurate for all of them.
rows.anchor: hepsinin vâzı‘ı Hak teâlâ olduğundan bunlara “kavânîn-i Hak” ve “sünnet-i ilâhiye” demek elbette daha doğrudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing divine laws is science; laws that lead to good are religion, community, or sharia. Seeking religion outside divine ordinance is false, yet not every divine law is religion: the law that a suicide dies is real, but suicide is evil; good-conforming acts are religious, evil-conforming ones contrary to religion.
rows.anchor: Bu kanunları bilmeye “ilm u fen” denildiği gibi, onların hayra götürenlerine de “din”, “millet”, “şeri‘at” ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human-made laws cannot constitute true science or religion; people should discover and reveal God's laws rather than legislate them. Archimedes, Newton, Aristotle, and Abu Hanifa discovered laws rather than inventing them.
rows.anchor: beşerin hakkı gerek ilimde ve gerek dinde kanun vaz‘etmek değil, Hakk’ın kanunlarını arayıp bulmak ve keşf u izhâr etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since divinely established laws are straight, “straight path” also conveys a clear, busy main road for revealing hidden laws and avoiding crooked human inventions unrelated to divine aid.
rows.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ ise vâzıh mânasını dahi tazammun ettiğinden bunları izhâra vesile olacak vâzıh ve işlek bir tarîk-i esâsîyi ifham ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance's orientation to good does not erase the laws that lead to evil; it frames good laws positively as commands and evil laws negatively as prohibitions, and the following verse's favored/not-angered/not-astray clauses show both aspects.
rows.anchor: hayr kanunlarını evâmir olarak müsbet ve şer kanunlarını nevâhî olarak menfî bir haysiyetle takyid etmeyi îcab edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the definite article marking the covenant path, verse 6 is a complete definition of the true religion and the following material explains it.
rows.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ lâm-ı ‘ahd ile dîn-i hakkın hadd-i tâmmıdır. Mâba‘di de bunun şerhidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In'am means giving and conveying a blessing; connecting it with “ala” conveys the Benefactor's exaltedness and the blessing's loftiness.
rows.anchor: “İn‘âm”, nimet vermek, nimeti îsâl etmektir. Aslında müte‘addîdir. Lâkin tafdil mânasını tazammun ile mün‘imin ulviyetini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ni'ma first means a pleasurable state or bliss and then anything that causes it; it relates to softness. A proverb says some have wealth but no enjoyment, like someone with bread who cannot taste it; true blessing includes the ability to enjoy.
rows.anchor: nice nimet sâhibi vardır ki tena‘‘umu yoktur. Meselâ ekmeği vardır yiyemez, yerse tadını bulamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted; they may broadly be considered as worldly or afterlife blessings.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın nimetleri ise sayılamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly blessings are bestowed or acquired: bestowed gifts include spiritual and bodily capacities, while acquired gifts include moral purification, knowledge, virtue, social standing, and wealth.
rows.anchor: Ni‘am-ı dünyeviye iki kısımdır: Vehbî, kesbî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife blessings include forgiveness, attaining God's pleasure, and eternal repose in the highest station with the nearest angels; they too divide into bestowed/acquired and spiritual/physical forms.
rows.anchor: Ni‘am-ı uhreviye, dünyada vâki‘olan ifrat ve tefritlerini mağfiret ederek rızâsına erdirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An apparent present blessing may later become a calamity, and an apparent hardship may become happiness; real happiness is what ends safely, so the request is for blessings that bring a safe outcome rather than immediate pleasure.
rows.anchor: ciddî ve hakīkī olan ni‘met ü saâdet âkıbeti her hâlde sâlim olanlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification that excludes anger and misguidance restricts the potentially all-inclusive favor to lasting good: afterlife blessings and their worldly precursors, especially life, liberty, faith, sound conscience, good character, social rectitude, beneficial knowledge, and righteous action.
rows.anchor: Bunların başı da hakk-ı hayat, hakk-ı hürriyet, iman, selâmet-i vicdan, hüsn-i ahlâk, salâh-ı ictimâ‘î, ilm-i nâfi‘, amel-i sâlihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic usage, liberty means owning one's rights, as explained in Kashf al-Pazdawi; its opposite is enslavement through another's ownership of those rights.
rows.anchor: Lisân-ı İslâm’da “hürriyet”, hukūkuna mâlikiyet diye târif olunur (Keşf-i Pezdevî)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rights originate in divine ordinance; if human law can alter or control them without consent, a person is partly enslaved and duties depend on another's arbitrary will rather than right.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir ferdin vaz‘-ı ilâhî olan hukūku kendi rızâsı munzam olmaksızın diğer bir vaz‘-ı beşerî ile tebdil, tağyir veya tasarrufa mahkum olabiliyorsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liberty cannot coherently belong to someone who rejects God or serves another; its guarantee lies in worshipping God alone. The straight path begins in servitude to God, aims first at the great worldly blessing of liberty, rests on life and faith, and depends on divine aid and guidance.
rows.anchor: Ve bunun için damân-ı hürriyet yalnız Allah’a ubûdiyettedir. Ve sırât-ı müstakīmin mebde’i bu ubûdiyet
